newsitem.title: UK: Foreign sales ruled out for British lottery.
newsitem.headline: Foreign sales ruled out for British lottery.

text.p: British lottery operator Camelot will not be allowed to extend the sale of tickets for its twice-weekly games overseas, a government minister said Sunday.
National Heritage Minister Virginia Bottomley said that any plans by Camelot to expand ticket sales abroad would be blocked by the lottery regulator Oflot.
"I don't think there's any question of people overseas playing our national lottery," she told British television.

"It's very carefully regulated. There's no question of people overseas playing, the regulator wouldn't be able to ensure propriety, he wouldn't be able to ensure, above all, that the players are protected," she added.
Camelot is jointly owned by Cadbury Schweppes Plc, De La Rue Plc, GTECH UK, Rascal Electronics and ICL.
